# Offisio

> Offisio is an office listing and booking agent for Egypt, built solo for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Indie track). An owner uploads a short walkthrough video of an office; the app surveys every space, decides which uses the layout suits (office, coworking, training, clinic, dental clinic, law office), writes a bilingual Arabic/English listing, and renders the room empty and fitted out. Renters book by chatting in Egyptian Arabic or English, on the website or on WhatsApp (text or voice notes), and pay in XPay test mode. Every AI call in the product goes to the Meta Model API (`https://api.meta.ai/v1`). Everything was written during the hackathon (Oct 26 - Nov 4, 2026), starting from an empty `create-next-app` scaffold; the git history is the record of work.

This is the long version of https://offisio.vercel.app/llms.txt. It inlines the essential content of the repo docs so a reader does not need to open them. Where this file and the code disagree, the code wins.

- Live site: https://offisio.vercel.app (English, LTR, default) and https://offisio.vercel.app/ar (Arabic, RTL)
- Source: https://github.com/Mohamedzh/offisio (branch `master`)
- Stack: Next.js 16 (App Router), TypeScript strict, Tailwind 4, pnpm; Postgres on Neon; Vercel Blob for media; QStash for post-upload steps; deployed on Vercel.

## 1. What we built

Demo loop:

1. Owner uploads a short office video.
2. The app extracts frames and produces structured specs (spaces, sizes, finishes, windows, plumbing).
3. The app generates a bilingual listing (Arabic RTL / English LTR, toggle on every page).
4. The app produces restaged photos: furniture removed, then fitted out for each use the layout suits.
5. A renter books through a chat agent in Egyptian Arabic or English, on the web or on WhatsApp.

Features (from the README "What we built" section):

- Video pipeline (QStash steps in `lib/pipeline/jobs.ts`): frames -> survey of every space -> deterministic use rubric -> specs -> bilingual listing -> AI empty room -> fit-out renders per passing use. Three units are real filmed offices; the other ten demo units are AI-generated and badged.
- Three rental tracks: furnished units can be booked by the day or the month; semifinished units are long-term only (the renter does the fit-out).
- Booking: daily day-slots (hourly underneath), atomic double-book protection, a 30-minute unpaid hold, an Egyptian-Arabic chat agent with venue add-ons, "what's near to eat" (`nearby_places`) and "near AUC"-style landmark search (19 hand-typed landmarks with Arabic/English aliases, sorted by straight-line distance).
- Add-ons: provided by the venue at our own demo prices (`lib/addons/catalog.ts`; prices always come from the catalogue, never the request): house coffee, tea, water, croissants and a sandwich tray on day bookings only, plus room extras (extra chair, whiteboard, printing).
- Nearby places: the two nearest cafes/restaurants within 1 km of each unit from the Google Places API (name, distance, Google Maps link, attribution). The renter orders from them directly; Offisio takes no food orders.
- WhatsApp channel: the same booking agent on WhatsApp (email-only booking, "what are my bookings", paid notice after the payment webhook) plus voice notes: ffmpeg converts the OGG/Opus note to WAV and `muse-voice-transcribe-1.0` transcribes it; the reply shows what was heard.
- Optional "Get updates on WhatsApp" link on the booking page for website bookings, so the paid notice and "my bookings" also work for them.
- Web chat mic: the browser records (MediaRecorder), `POST /api/chat/voice` runs the limits, ffmpeg (whitelisted input formats and protocols) and `muse-voice-transcribe-1.0` on `meta.product`, then the same agent turn as typed chat (`lib/web-chat.ts`), and returns the transcript with the reply.
- Guest uploads: upload needs no sign-in. A signed `offisio_guest` cookie (random id, not PII, 7 days) makes the upload a private draft (`units.guest_owner` set, `owner_wa_id` null): not listed, not bookable, invisible to the agent, `noindex`, with a "Draft, not listed yet" banner; only the uploading browser can edit or stage it. "Publish with WhatsApp" signs in, then `POST /api/units/<slug>/publish` moves the draft to the owner's number. "Try it with a sample walkthrough" on `/upload` runs the real pipeline on our own filmed 20 s video with editable pre-filled details.
- AI listing review: after the listing step, a `review` step (`muse-spark-1.3` via `meta.nonPii`, `LISTING_REVIEW_PROMPT_V2`, validated JSON, cached in `ai_cache` by text) proofreads the bilingual title and description: typos, natural Egyptian Arabic, English mixed into Arabic, claims the specs don't back (wrong numbers are corrected to the spec value), Arabic/English disagreement, contact details, pushy tone. The owner sees the issues on the draft and edit pages and can apply the fixes in one click (`POST /api/units/<slug>/review/apply`, owner only, writes only the cached corrected text) or run it again after a specs edit (`POST /api/units/<slug>/review`). Advisory only: publishing is never blocked. Upload also refuses contact details typed into district or floor (`CONTACT_INFO_NOT_ALLOWED`).
- Near me: tap 📍 in web chat (browser location) or share a location pin on WhatsApp, then ask for an office near you. The server validates and rounds the location (about 100 m, coarse Egypt box, fixed codes `LOCATION_BAD` / `LOCATION_OUTSIDE_EGYPT`), keeps it in the chat session only (`loc` on user messages in `chat_sessions.messages`, no migration), never logs it and never sends coordinates to the model. `search_units` gains `near_me` + `radius_km` (default 10 km, 1-50): results nearest first with approximate straight-line distances; if nothing is in range the agent says so and offers the 3 nearest. With no location yet, the agent asks for a pin (WhatsApp) or the 📍 button (web). Booking agent prompt `AGENT_PROMPT_V9`. Acceptance scenarios 14-18 pass.
- Owner sign-in with WhatsApp: the site gives a one-time code, the owner sends it from WhatsApp and confirms with YES; sign-in is needed to publish a draft, only the owner can save edits, and "Offisio logout" signs out everywhere.
- List an office from WhatsApp (section 7): the owner sends a walkthrough video to the Offisio number, the bot collects the missing details by chat (text, voice note or location pin), creates the same guest draft as a web upload, runs the same pipeline and sends a single-use link to the draft; "publish" / "انشر" lists it under the sender's number.
- Run from the repo: `docker-compose.yml` (Postgres 16), `pnpm seed` loads the 13 demo units from `data/seed/demo-snapshot.json`, local media in `public/uploads/` without a Blob token, and fixed `*_NOT_CONFIGURED` codes for missing integrations (section 2, Run locally).
- Demo listings are preview-only: any visitor can try the edit form; changes show only in their own browser and the real listing (and the agent) never changes.
- Payments (test mode): XPay hosted checkout plus a signature-verified webhook; a booking confirms only on the webhook.
- Media on Vercel Blob: frames and renders, browser-direct uploads via `/api/blob/upload` (or `/api/blob/local` in local media mode), listing photos served from the `media` table.
- Homepage: decorative `muse-image-1.0` paper-collage illustrations (`public/home/`; generated by `scripts/generate-home-art.ts`, removed later, see git history), always labelled decorative and kept separate from real listing photos.

### Scope

In scope: the demo loop above, plus these owner-approved additions: payments in XPay test mode only (booking confirms on a signed webhook); owner sign-in (built as WhatsApp sign-in; renters stay guests); a required per-unit location and "near X" search for the agent; nearby cafes/restaurants per unit via the Google Places API; long post-upload steps chained with QStash; venue add-ons; renter booking over WhatsApp via the Meta WhatsApp Cloud API with XPay test-mode payment links; WhatsApp voice notes; guest uploads as private drafts (publishing needs WhatsApp sign-in); the web chat mic (`muse-voice-transcribe-1.0` on `meta.product`); listing an office by sending a video on WhatsApp.

Out of scope (not built, even partially): live payments, cash on delivery, partial payments, standalone food orders, accounts beyond owner sign-in, reviews, map search UI, host analytics, mobile apps, a separate backend service, live scraping of any third-party site.

### How it was built

Development was split roughly half and half between a Muse-model agent workflow and Claude models via Claude Code. Both are development tools only; every model call a user triggers runs on Meta models via the Meta Model API.

- Architecture and planning: a main session on `muse-wonder-1.0` writes segment briefs under `docs/plan/`, reviews diffs and makes ship/fix calls.
- Implementation, tests and review: `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` agents implement one brief at a time, write and run tests, and review diffs against the project rules. Contributor agents only touch synthetic data, because contributor content may be used for training.
- Claude models (via Claude Code) did audits, planning passes and implementation alongside.
- Role definitions: `docs/agents/` (architect/planner, implementor, test writer and runner, reviewer, QA integrity, QA UI, QA head reviewer, plus media-capability test roles).
- Work is split into segment files `docs/plan/00-foundation.md` to `docs/plan/07-judge-access.md`; each records status, decisions, verification evidence and a handoff. These files and the git history are the record of work.

## 2. Testing (for judges)

Everything below runs on the live site with no setup and no real money. Payments run in XPay test mode (a TEST MODE banner shows at checkout). Chat, upload, web mic, language and preview edits also run on a local copy (Run locally, below). For scripted checks see section 15.

Start at https://offisio.vercel.app and browse the listings, or open a bookable unit such as https://offisio.vercel.app/en/units/gen-alex-chatby (EGP 600/day). Listings whose photos are AI-generated are badged "Demo listing — AI-generated photos, not a filmed office"; the first three units are filmed real offices.

### Test card (XPay test mode)

The card number is always the same; the expiry date chooses the outcome.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Card number | `5123 4500 0000 0008` |
| Cardholder name | `Test Account` (anything works) |
| CVV | `100` |
| Expiry `01/39` | Approved |
| Expiry `05/39` | Declined |
| Expiry `01/27` | Insufficient funds |
| Expiry `04/27` | Expired card |

After clicking Pay, a 3D Secure emulator appears: leave "(Y) Authentication Successful" selected and click Submit.

### Flows to try

1. Book + pay (approved). On a unit page pick a free day, enter any name, an `01...` mobile number and an email, Confirm & pay, then Pay now with expiry `01/39`. You return to the booking page; within a few seconds the status flips to confirmed. Confirmation comes only from the payment webhook, never from the redirect, so refreshing before it lands still shows `awaiting_payment`.
2. Declined card. Same flow with expiry `05/39`. Checkout shows "Payment declined" and the booking stays `awaiting_payment`. Retrying with `01/39` on the same session succeeds.
3. Chat booking. Open Chat and write, for example, `عايز مكتب في الزمالك ليوم واحد` or `I want an office in Zamalek for one day`. The agent searches real availability, quotes the total and collects contact details. Try `I want an office near AUC` for landmark search.
4. Nearby places and add-ons. Each unit page lists the two nearest cafes/restaurants within 1 km. Add-ons (house coffee & snacks on day bookings, room extras) are itemised on the same payment.
5. Owner upload (no sign-in). `/upload`: add a short office video, or tap "Try it with a sample walkthrough". The app extracts frames, surveys the spaces, generates specs and a bilingual listing and renders fit-outs. The result is a private draft ("Draft, not listed yet"), reachable by direct link only. "Publish with WhatsApp" signs you in and lists it. On a local copy without WhatsApp (`WHATSAPP_TOKEN` unset, not on Vercel) the button is a labelled local demo publish.
6. Language / RTL. Toggle عربي (top corner): every page mirrors to RTL; English is LTR.
7. WhatsApp. Message the Offisio WhatsApp number shown on the site, in text or as a voice note. Ask for an office, book, then ask "what are my bookings". In web Chat, tap the mic, speak up to 60 s and tap again; the transcript appears as your message, then the agent replies.
8. Owner sign-in. See section 8.
9. Demo edits. On a demo listing, try the owner edit form: your changes show only in your browser (with a Reset bar), and the real listing never changes.
10. List from WhatsApp. Send a walkthrough video (up to 45 s) to the Offisio WhatsApp number, then the location pin (or a Maps link), monthly rent, floor and district in text or a voice note. The bot asks only for what is missing, analyzes the video and sends a single-use link to your draft; reply "publish" / "انشر" to list it under your number.

### Local checks

```bash
pnpm lint        # 0 errors expected
pnpm typecheck   # tsc --noEmit
pnpm build       # production build
pnpm chat-acceptance  # 13 scripted conversations against the real agent (paid model calls)
```

Notes: no real money moves anywhere. Test bookings write to the demo database and can be deleted. Phone numbers, names and chat text in tests are demo data and are only ever sent to `muse-spark-1.3`. Payment evidence from the 2026-10-29 live run (approved -> confirmed, declined -> stayed unconfirmed) is in `docs/plan/05-demo-polish.md`.

### Run locally

```bash
pnpm install
docker compose up -d          # Postgres 16 on 127.0.0.1:5432, user/password/db all "offisio"
cp .env.example .env.local    # set META_API_KEY, DATABASE_URL, DATABASE_URL_POOLED
pnpm migrate
pnpm seed
pnpm dev                      # http://localhost:3000
```

- With Docker both URLs are `postgres://offisio:offisio@localhost:5432/offisio`. Any Postgres 13+ works; SSL is off for localhost or `?sslmode=disable`. `pnpm seed` refuses a non-local database unless run with `--remote`.
- The seed (`scripts/seed.ts`, idempotent, one transaction) loads `data/seed/demo-snapshot.json`: the 13 demo units with specs, listings, media rows (public Blob URLs) and nearby place ids. Availability is regenerated from today through the later of 2026-12-15 or today + 60 days. Seeded units have no owner.
- Places: the snapshot stores only `place_id` and our distance (Google terms). With `GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY` set, the seed refetches the names (one Nearby Search per unit, 13 calls); `--no-places` skips it. Without the key, the unit page shows "Place nearby" with a Maps link.
- Minimum env: `META_API_KEY` + `DATABASE_URL`. Missing integrations return fixed codes, shown translated: `XPAY_NOT_CONFIGURED` (checkout, 503), `WHATSAPP_NOT_CONFIGURED` (sign-in, 503), `PLACES_NOT_CONFIGURED` (the upload `places` step).
- Local media: with no `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN` and not on Vercel, the browser PUTs frames and the video to `/api/blob/local`; files and renders land in gitignored `public/uploads/<slug>/`.
- Without QStash, pipeline steps run in-process (no automatic retries; the edit page has a retry button).
- Status: the seed was tested in a rolled-back temporary schema; `docker compose up` itself was not yet run on the dev machine.

## 3. Architecture overview

```
Browser (Next.js)                 Server (route handlers + QStash steps)          Meta Model API
Video upload -> frames (canvas) -> upload: unit row + frames on Blob
                                   analyze: survey of spaces ------------------->  muse-spark-1.3
                                            rubric (code, deterministic)
                                   listing: specs + AR/EN copy ----------------->  muse-spark-1.3
                                   stage:<style>: empty, then fit-out ---------->  muse-image-1.0 (edits)
                                   places: nearby food (Google Places API)
Listing page  <- Postgres (units, media, availability, bookings, payments, chat_sessions)
Web chat ------------------------> booking agent (native tool calling) -------->  muse-spark-1.3
Web mic -> /api/chat/voice ------> ffmpeg -> transcription -> same agent ------>  muse-voice-transcribe-1.0
WhatsApp (text / voice note) ----> webhook -> ffmpeg -> transcription ---------->  muse-voice-transcribe-1.0
                                           -> same booking agent ------------->  muse-spark-1.3
WhatsApp owner video ------------> webhook -> ffmpeg frames + Blob -> owner details ->  muse-spark-1.3 (meta.product)
                                           -> guest draft -> same pipeline -> single-use link
XPay hosted checkout ------------> signed webhook -> confirm booking -> WhatsApp paid notice
```

Layout:

- `app/[lang]/...`: every page lives under `/en` or `/ar`; `proxy.ts` redirects unprefixed paths to the saved or default locale (English).
- `app/api/...`: route handlers (chat + chat voice, bookings, availability, add-ons, payments checkout + webhook, WhatsApp webhook, auth login/logout/status, units upload/specs/stage/pipeline/publish, blob upload + local, pipeline steps).
- `lib/meta/`: the Meta client and all prompts (the only place model IDs and prompts live).
- `lib/pipeline/`: `survey.ts`, `rubric.ts`, `specs-listing.ts`, `staging.ts`, `ingest.ts`, `jobs.ts`, `cache.ts`. Each step is an idempotent `pipeline_jobs` row and one QStash message; a failed render never blocks the listing or other renders.
- `lib/agent/agent.ts`: booking agent; `lib/booking.ts`: booking creation and confirmation; `lib/db/`: schema and queries.
- `lib/whatsapp.ts`, `lib/audio.ts`, `lib/web-chat.ts`, `lib/wa-listing.ts` + `lib/video-frames.ts` + `lib/wa-link.ts` + `lib/upload-unit.ts` (WhatsApp video listing), `lib/login.ts`, `lib/owner.ts`, `lib/xpay.ts`, `lib/places.ts`, `lib/guard.ts`, `lib/blob.ts` (Blob or local media).

Key design decisions:

- Meta models only in the product's AI; no other provider or SDK in any request path.
- Structured output wherever a model feeds code (survey, specs, listing JSON; agent tool arguments), validated before use.
- One pipeline, explicit steps, persisted status; each step re-runnable alone. Image edits are cached by base-image bytes plus prompt text, so re-runs cost nothing.
- Remove first, then restage from the empty room, so walls and windows stay consistent across uses. Semifinished shells are rendered finished (floor, ceiling, paint) because the renter fits them out; geometry stays fixed.
- The source video is stored on Vercel Blob for playback; frames are extracted in the browser and uploaded directly to Blob (avoids the function body limit); only frames reach the model.
- Survey from frames at about 1 per second (at most 30), not from the video URL: a direct `video_url` call worked in testing but its sampling missed one of two rooms.
- English is the default locale (for judges), with a full Arabic RTL variant of every page under `/ar`; layouts use logical CSS properties so they mirror.
- Precompute for the demo: the 13 seeded units are fully processed ahead of time; the live upload path runs the same pipeline.

### Data model (Postgres on Neon, `lib/db/schema.sql`)

- `units`: slug, kind (furnished / semifinished), status, district, monthly rent, daily price, floor, rental tracks (daily / monthly / long_term), bilingual title, summary and highlights, location (lat/lng, approximate flag), owner WhatsApp id for published uploads, `guest_owner` (random browser id) while an upload is a draft.
- `specs`: specs JSON per unit (including the rubric use verdicts), with the model that produced it.
- `media`: video, keyframes and staged renders (kind, style, Blob URL, `is_current`).
- `availability`: day/hour slots per unit with an `is_booked` flag, unique per start time.
- `bookings`: unit, slots, track, renter name/phone/email (PII), WhatsApp id (WhatsApp bookings only), totals, status (`awaiting_payment` until the verified webhook), `created_via` (`chat` for web chat and the booking form, `whatsapp`).
- `booking_addons`: item id, bilingual name, quantity, unit price from the catalogue.
- `payments`: provider `xpay`, checkout session id, amount, webhook-driven status.
- `chat_sessions`: session key (random UUID on web; hashed sender + Cairo day on WhatsApp), messages, tool calls, turn count.
- `pipeline_jobs`: one row per unit and step (queued / running / done / failed, attempts, last error).
- `unit_places`: Google place id, name (null for seeded rows until refetched with a key), type, distance, Maps link.
- `usage_counters`: daily counters for rate limits, token usage and estimated spend (hashed keys).
- `ai_cache`: cached model results keyed by input content and prompt version.
- `login_codes`, `owner_epochs`: owner sign-in codes and per-number sign-out epochs.
- `wa_listing_drafts`: one row per WhatsApp listing video: sender WhatsApp id (PII, never logged), unit slug, random guest id, video and frame URLs, collected fields (JSON), language, status (`collecting` / `processing` / `ready` / `published` / `expired`).

### Decision log highlights (from `docs/DESIGN.md` and `docs/plan/06-judge-ready.md`)

- 2026-10-27: SAM 3.1 dropped; prompt-guided `muse-image-1.0` removal passed on furnished and bare units.
- 2026-10-27: three-track rental catalogue (furnished daily + monthly; semifinished long-term only).
- 2026-10-27: payments brought into scope in test mode only; booking confirms only on a verified webhook.
- 2026-10-27: Neon Postgres live (direct URL for migrations, pooled URL for the app).
- 2026-10-29: payment provider switched from Paymob to XPay (Paymob's test integration had no working acquirer credentials); XPay approved and declined runs verified live.
- 2026-10-29: source video upload to Blob allowed (frames still extracted in the browser); English stays the default locale.
- 2026-10-29: `muse-image-1.0` returns WebP and edits reject a mismatched declared MIME type, so staging sniffs the real type.
- 2026-10-30: use rubric replaces single-room specs; native tool calling replaces the JSON-action agent; guardrails and spend breaker added.
- 2026-10-31: location, Google Places nearby and QStash pipeline steps approved; WhatsApp booking channel approved.
- 2026-11-02: WhatsApp sign-in replaces Clerk; WhatsApp renter identity (sender id + email); voice notes reopened and built; demo listings made preview-only.
- 2026-11-02: third-party demo menu data removed after organizer guidance.
- 2026-11-02: after organizer guidance that the project must run from the public repo and be testable without credentials: guest uploads as private drafts (publish needs WhatsApp sign-in), a seed snapshot + Docker Postgres, local media mode, a sample walkthrough and the web chat mic (`docs/plan/07-judge-access.md`).

## 4. Meta models and routing (PII table)

All product model calls go to `https://api.meta.ai/v1`. Model IDs are defined only in `lib/meta/client.ts`, which exposes three paths; no other code picks a model ID.

| Path | Model | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `meta.product.chat` | `muse-spark-1.3` (never contributor) | Booking agent, web chat and WhatsApp; owner details from WhatsApp listing messages (`chatOnce`: one try, 20 s) (PII) |
| `meta.product.transcribe` | `muse-voice-transcribe-1.0` | WhatsApp voice notes and the web chat mic, `POST /v1/asr/transcribe` (multipart `request` JSON + `audio` WAV) |
| `meta.nonPii.chat` | `muse-spark-1.3` in production | Space survey, specs, bilingual listing |
| `meta.imageEdit` | `muse-image-1.0` | Empty-room and fit-out renders (`/v1/images/edits`) |
| `meta.imageGenerate` | `muse-image-1.0` | AI-generated demo listing photos and decorative art (`/v1/images/generations`), synthetic only |
| `meta.public.chat` | `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, or Muse Spark Open locally | Public/synthetic development data only (for example a QA gate in `scripts/generate-units.ts`) |

Routing rules (from AGENTS.md):

| Data class | Examples | Allowed model | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Public / synthetic | Test prompts, fake units, demo footage we shot, style prompts | `muse-spark-1.3` or `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` | Contributor content may train Meta models, so nothing private goes there |
| Product data, no PII | Frames of empty/furnished rooms, specs JSON, listing copy, style prompts | `muse-spark-1.3`, `muse-image-1.0` | Normal product path |
| PII | Renter name, phone, email, chat transcripts, voice notes, owner contact details | `muse-spark-1.3` only; voice-note audio also to `muse-voice-transcribe-1.0`. Never contributor | Contributor content may be used for training |

Development switch: `OFFISIO_DEV_MODELS=modal` sends non-PII calls (survey, specs, listing) to our own Muse Spark Open deployment on Modal (open-weight Meta model, `meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B`); `=contributor` uses `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`. Only for local runs on our own or synthetic footage. The switch is ignored whenever `VERCEL` is set, so production always uses `muse-spark-1.3`, and chat never switches. Seeded demo data was generated on `muse-spark-1.3`.

Transcription details: the API accepts only RIFF/WAVE mono 16-bit PCM at 16 or 24 kHz; WhatsApp sends OGG/Opus and browsers record webm/ogg Opus or mp4 AAC, so `lib/audio.ts` converts with ffmpeg (`ffmpeg-static`, `-ac 1 -ar 24000 -c:a pcm_s16le`, 10 s kill, `-protocol_whitelist file,pipe` and a demuxer whitelist). Voice notes and web mic uploads are capped at 1 MB; the web mic also at 60 s. Audio and transcripts are never logged; errors carry the HTTP status only.

Not used: `sam-3.1`. It was dropped on 2026-10-27 because no callable segmentation endpoint was found in the OpenAI-shaped API, and prompt-guided `muse-image-1.0` edits passed on the furnished and bare units. Meta's docs show SAM callable via `/v1/responses`; we found that after choosing edits and did not test it.

## 5. Space survey and use rubric

Source: `docs/RUBRIC.md` (`RUBRIC_V1`, owner-approved 2026-10-30). It decides which uses an office fits from its whole walkthrough. Only passing uses get fit-out renders. It is not a licensing check: verdicts say the layout suits a use, and every verdict is shown as an AI estimate.

Two stages:

1. Survey (`muse-spark-1.3`, `SURVEY_PROMPT_V1`). Input: frames at about 1 per second (at most 30, long side 1024 px) in walk order, each labelled with index and timestamp. Output per distinct space: type (entrance, corridor, room, bathroom, kitchenette, storage, balcony, other), estimated width x length and confidence, windows and light, plumbing seen, finish and furnishing, frames where visible plus the best frame, and adjacency.
2. Rules (code, `lib/pipeline/rubric.ts`). Deterministic thresholds on the survey, so a verdict is reproducible and explainable. Reasons are code templates in Arabic and English, never free model text.

Verdicts: fits; fits after fit-out (partitions could create missing rooms; bathroom and plumbing must already exist); not suitable (with the reason).

| Use | Needs |
|---|---|
| Private / startup office | at least 1 usable room of 6 m2 or more; a window or AC |
| Open-plan / coworking | largest room 25 m2 or more |
| Meeting / training room | a room of 15 m2 or more |
| General clinic | exam room 9 m2 or more, separate waiting space 6 m2 or more, a bathroom (fit-out route: one room of 16 m2 or more to split, plus a bathroom) |
| Dental clinic | general clinic plus a prep/sterilisation area of 2 m2 or more (or the bathroom retrofitted as prep = fits after fit-out) |
| Accounting / law office | reception 6 m2 or more plus a private office of 7 m2 or more (fit-out route: one room of 14 m2 or more to split) |

Capacity: desk 120 x 70 cm; comfortable about 4.0 m2 per desk, maximum about 3.0 m2 per desk of usable room area; a room counts only if at least 1.4 m wide and 1.9 m deep. Seats: classroom area / 1.9 m2, theatre area / 1.0 m2. Calibration: the filmed `full` office really holds 3 desks; `empty1`/`empty2` (2 rooms + bathroom + a small extra area) fit general and dental clinics. These are planning heuristics, not Ministry of Health figures.

## 6. Booking agent: tools and prompt versions

`lib/agent/agent.ts` runs a native tool-calling loop on `meta.product` (`muse-spark-1.3`), at most 6 tool rounds per turn. Tool arguments are validated in code; bad arguments go back to the model as an error result, never a 500. Units, prices, uses, capacities and free days come only from tool results.

Tools:

- `search_units`: filters `district`, `near` (a landmark; results sorted by distance), `use` (rubric use), `min_desks`, `max_rent_egp`, `track` (daily, monthly, long_term).
- `get_unit`: summary, specs, suitable uses with reasons, next free days.
- `nearby_places`: cafes and restaurants within 1 km (name, distance, Maps link) plus the venue add-ons with ids and prices.
- `check_availability`: whether a day is free for a daily booking, plus the next free days.
- `create_booking`: after the renter confirms; creates an unpaid booking held 30 minutes; takes `slug`, `date`, `track`, `renter_name`, `renter_email`, `renter_phone` (web only) and `addons`.
- `my_bookings` (WhatsApp only): the sender's own bookings with status and, for unpaid ones, the payment link. Not offered on web chat, because a typed phone number is not proof of identity.

Behaviour: replies follow the language of the renter's latest message (Egyptian Arabic, never formal MSA, or English); relative dates are resolved in Africa/Cairo time; at most 3 options are shown; a booking is called "held / awaiting payment" until the XPay webhook confirms it; place names follow the reply's language. The web chat shows up to 3 unit photo cards; WhatsApp sends one image message per unit.

Prompt version history (only V8 is live in `lib/meta/prompts.ts`; V3-V7 are summarised in its comments, earlier versions are in git history; names only):

- `AGENT_PROMPT_V1` (Oct 26): first booking prompt.
- `AGENT_PROMPT_V2` (Oct 30): native tool calling replaces the earlier one-JSON-action-per-turn agent.
- `AGENT_PROMPT_V3` (Nov 2): add-ons from `nearby_places`; `search_units` takes `near`.
- `AGENT_PROMPT_V4` (Nov 2): per-channel contact details (`{CHANNEL}` block); WhatsApp uses the sender's number and asks only for an email.
- `AGENT_PROMPT_V5` (Nov 2): reply language follows the latest message.
- `AGENT_PROMPT_V6` (Nov 2): "confirmed" only after payment; place names in the reply's language.
- `AGENT_PROMPT_V7` (Nov 2): friendly booking lists (title, date label, status, ref last).
- `AGENT_PROMPT_V8` (Nov 2, current): third-party menu data removed; `nearby_places` gives places only and add-ons are the venue's own.
- Other prompts: `SURVEY_PROMPT_V1`, `SPECS_PROMPT_V1`, `LISTING_PROMPT_V1`, `LISTING_PROMPT_V2` (mentions rubric uses, never claims licensing), `EMPTY_PROMPT_V1`, `STYLE_PROMPTS_V1`, `STAGE_PROMPTS_V3` (use-driven fit-out renders), channel blocks `AGENT_CHANNEL_WEB` and `AGENT_CHANNEL_WHATSAPP`.

Acceptance: `scripts/chat-acceptance.ts` runs 13 scripted Egyptian-Arabic/English booking conversations (11-13 on the WhatsApp channel) against the real agent with synthetic renters, writes transcripts locally and cleans up its bookings and sessions. Recorded runs are in `docs/plan/06-judge-ready.md` (for example 13/13 on V5, 12/13 on V7 with the failure analysed there).

## 7. WhatsApp channel

- Meta WhatsApp Cloud API on the owner's own business number. Judges: message the Offisio WhatsApp number shown on the site.
- `GET /api/whatsapp/webhook`: verification handshake. `POST`: returns 401 on a bad `X-Hub-Signature-256` HMAC; deduplicates by message id (survives Cairo midnight); runs the agent turn in `after()` so Meta gets a fast 200.
- Each text runs the same agent and tools as web chat with `created_via='whatsapp'`. Sessions are keyed by a hashed sender number. Replies go through the Cloud API inside the 24-hour customer-service window.
- Identity: the phone comes from the verified sender id (never asked); the name from the WhatsApp profile when Meta sends it; the agent asks only for an email. Non-Egyptian WhatsApp numbers can book.
- Proactive check: each turn the system prompt carries the sender's upcoming pending or confirmed bookings, so the agent mentions an existing booking before starting a new one.
- Voice notes: media lookup and download, ffmpeg to WAV, `muse-voice-transcribe-1.0`, then the agent; the reply shows what was heard. Forwarded audio files are not supported; long or failed notes get a fixed bilingual reply. Validated 2026-11-02 on a real 6-second Egyptian-Arabic note: the transcript was exact ("عايزة احجز مكتب النهاردة في العاصمة الادارية لشخص واحد شوف لي كده ايه المتاح واعمل لي الحجز"), and the reply was prompt and correct: an available unit in the New Administrative Capital, the house add-ons offered, an email-only ask and a photo card.
- Paid notice: after the signed XPay webhook confirms a booking (or marks it `paid_conflict`) and the booking has a WhatsApp sender, a short Arabic + English message goes out. Send failures are logged and never fail the webhook.
- Website bookings can opt in with "Get updates on WhatsApp": wa.me with a prefilled `Offisio <ref>-<code>`, where the code is an HMAC of the booking id; the webhook verifies it and links the sender, only if unlinked or the same sender.
- Limits: the same character, turn and per-sender rate limits as web chat.
- Owner listing by video: a video (mp4/3gp, up to 45 s and 16 MB; `wa_video` limit 3 per sender per day, plus the spend breaker) creates a `collecting` draft at once, then is downloaded (20 s timeout), cut into up to 20 JPEG keyframes by ffmpeg (input and protocol whitelists, 25 s) and stored under `uploads/<slug>/` like a web upload (15 s storage deadline). Details arrive as a location pin (Egypt box), a Maps link or "lat, lng", and rent / daily price / floor / district / kind / start date from text, a caption or a voice note, extracted by one `meta.product` call (`OWNER_DETAILS_PROMPT_V1`, one try, 20 s timeout, validated JSON, contact details refused). The bot confirms what it understood and asks only for what is missing. Complete: the unit is created as a guest draft (same path as the web upload) and the pipeline runs; after the review step the bot sends a single-use link (`/api/auth/wa-link`, HMAC-signed, 30 min, no phone number in the token, preview crawlers refused) that sets the guest and owner cookies and opens the draft page. Keywords: "publish" / "انشر", "cancel" / "إلغاء" (while collecting), "link" / "رابط", "status" / "حالة". Collecting and processing drafts expire after 24 h, ready drafts after 7 days. Worst-case video turn: about 105 s within the webhook's 120 s (a caption's short Maps link is not expanded; the bot asks for a pin or the full link).

## 8. Owner sign-in with WhatsApp

Replaces the planned Clerk sign-in (owner decision 2026-11-02; no new dependency). Renters stay guests.

1. On `/[lang]/login` (or inline on the upload page) the site issues a one-time code (8 Crockford base32 characters, valid 10 minutes, bound to the browser by an httpOnly nonce).
2. The owner sends `Offisio login XXXX-XXXX` to the Offisio WhatsApp number (the page offers a wa.me link).
3. The signed webhook marks the code pending for that sender and replies with a warning; the owner must reply YES (English or Egyptian Arabic) within 2 minutes.
4. The page then sets an HMAC-SHA256 signed 24-hour `offisio_owner` cookie carrying the sender id and a per-number sign-out epoch.
5. `Offisio logout` bumps the epoch and deletes pending codes, ending every session for that number.

Upload needs no sign-in. A signed-in owner's upload records the owner on the unit. Anyone else gets an HMAC-signed `offisio_guest` cookie (random id, not PII, 7 days, same signing scheme as the owner cookie) and the unit is a draft (`guest_owner` set, `owner_wa_id` null). Drafts are left out of the home listings, the `/api/units` list, the agent and booking; the unit page shows them by direct link with `noindex` and a "Draft, not listed yet" banner. Specs, stage and pipeline writes are allowed only for the unit's owner, or for a draft's uploading browser. Everyone else, and the 13 seeded demo units always, get a cookie-only preview.

Publishing a draft: the banner's "Publish with WhatsApp" goes to `/login?next=/<lang>/units/<slug>` (`next` accepts only `/(ar|en)/...` paths), then `POST /api/units/<slug>/publish` moves the draft to the signed-in number and clears `guest_owner`. When WhatsApp is not configured (`WHATSAPP_TOKEN` unset) and not on Vercel, the button is a labelled local demo publish: it sets the non-numeric sentinel owner `local-demo` (it can never match a real owner) and keeps `guest_owner`, so the browser can still edit. On Vercel without WhatsApp, publishing is shown as unavailable. Audio, transcripts, phone numbers and login codes are never logged; errors log only a code. The browser only sees a masked number. `OWNER_SESSION_SECRET` must be set on Vercel (owner sign-in refuses to work without it there). Sign-in attempts are rate limited per browser IP and per sender.

## 9. Payment flow

1. A booking (form, web chat or WhatsApp) is created as an unpaid hold for 30 minutes (`BOOKING_HOLD_MINUTES`). Day-slot inserts are atomic, so two renters cannot book the same day.
2. Checkout creates an XPay Checkout Session (test mode); the renter pays on the hosted page and is redirected back to the booking page.
3. The redirect never confirms anything. `POST /api/payments/webhook` verifies the `xpay-signature` HMAC (timestamp + raw body, constant-time compare) and returns 401 on mismatch.
4. A paid event confirms the booking (or marks `paid_conflict` if the slot was lost); a failed event leaves it unconfirmed. WhatsApp bookings then get the paid notice.
5. Add-on prices come only from `lib/addons/catalog.ts`; a price in the request is ignored, and house food and drinks are accepted only on day bookings.

Out of scope by rule: live payments, cash on delivery, partial payments, standalone food orders.

## 10. Data & rights

- Filmed units (`full`, `empty1`, `empty2`): phone walkthroughs shot by the owner, not stock. Stored on Vercel Blob, not in the repo (`public/demo` is gitignored).
- Every other listing photo, the fit-out renders and the homepage illustrations are generated by `muse-image-1.0` and labelled (listing badge "Demo listing — AI-generated photos, not a filmed office"; homepage art marked decorative).
- Brand assets (logo, wordmark, app icons) come from our own hand-drawn sources in `public/brand`, rendered by `scripts/brand-assets.ts`.
- Nearby places: Google Places API (Nearby Search, official API) with "Places from Google Maps" attribution. Only the fields we display are stored (place ID, name, type, distance, Maps link). The repo's seed snapshot holds only place ids and our own distances (Places terms allow caching only the id); names are refetched with your own key at seed time.
- No third-party menu data. An early demo used menu data collected from a public site; it was removed on 2026-11-02 after organizer guidance (use only data we have rights to). Files, import scripts, the database table and brand matching are removed from the current code (they remain visible in the public git history: added in `2f0f0fa`, removed in `35c37e1`; the owner chose not to rewrite history so the commit record stays intact). Add-ons are the venue's own items at our demo prices.
- All tests and acceptance runs use synthetic renters (fake names, numbers and emails); test bookings and sessions are cleaned up.
- No secrets in the repo (it is public). Keys are environment variables only; names are listed in `.env.example` (for example `META_API_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, `DATABASE_URL_POOLED`, `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN`, `XPAY_SECRET_KEY`, `XPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET`, `OWNER_SESSION_SECRET`, `GUARD_SALT`, `GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY`, `QSTASH_TOKEN`).
- Apart from the removed menu data above, no code, data or assets were copied from other projects.

## 11. Safety & limits

PII handling:

- Anything containing a name, phone, email, chat text or audio is routed only to `muse-spark-1.3` (`meta.product`), plus `muse-voice-transcribe-1.0` for audio. Never the contributor model. Enforced by the client structure in `lib/meta/client.ts`.
- The booking GET API does not return renter name, phone, email or WhatsApp id. Web chat rejects WhatsApp-style session ids and uses random UUIDs.
- Rate-limit counters store hashed client IPs (salted with `GUARD_SALT`, which fails closed on Vercel), never raw addresses.
- Audio, transcripts, phone numbers and login codes are never logged; errors log only a code (for example `WHATSAPP_SEND_400`).

Rate limits and caps (`lib/guard.ts`, defaults, each overridable by env), per hashed IP or sender / global per day:

| Kind | Per caller | Global |
|---|---|---|
| chat | 40 | 1000 |
| upload | 3 | 20 |
| image_edit | 4 | 40 |
| booking | 5 | 100 |
| blob_token | 100 | 1000 |
| blob_video (video upload tokens, guests allowed) | 3 | 20 |
| voice (web mic; also counts as a chat turn) | 15 | 300 |
| wa_video (WhatsApp listing videos, per sender) | 3 | 30 |
| wa_link | 5 | 200 |
| spec_edit | 30 | 500 |
| login (per IP) / wa_login (per sender) | 10 | - (per caller only) |
| wa_logout (per sender) | 20 | - (per caller only) |

Caps: 800 characters per message, 20 turns per session, video up to 45 s and 80 MB, 3 to 30 frames of at most 1 MB each, web mic audio up to 1 MB and 60 s.

Spend breaker: every model response's usage is priced from Meta list prices and summed per Cairo day. When estimated spend reaches `DEMO_DAILY_SPEND_USD` (default USD 15), uploads, staging and web mic turns are blocked; browsing, booking, payment and cached units keep working. Calls to our own Modal deployment count as zero Meta spend.

Webhooks: XPay and WhatsApp webhooks are HMAC-verified and return 401 on a bad signature; WhatsApp messages are deduplicated by message id.

Payments: XPay test mode only; no real money.

## 12. Known limitations

- Owner sign-in is exposed to code-relay phishing (tricking someone into sending a code from their WhatsApp); the YES warning mitigates this but does not eliminate it.
- Districts are stored in English only; the agent translates them in Arabic replies, and the Arabic location line on unit pages still mixes English (for example "Zamalek, Cairo · أدوار 4th").
- The browser's own form validation bubble is English on `/ar`.
- SAM 3.1 is not used (see section 4); Meta's docs show it callable via `/v1/responses`, untested by us.
- Survey sizes, use verdicts and desk capacity are AI estimates of the layout, not a licensing or measurement check.
- Voice is validated on one real Egyptian-Arabic WhatsApp note (2026-11-02, exact transcript, correct reply; section 7) and the web mic on a synthetic text-to-speech clip; there is no broad accuracy study.
- A guest draft is tied to one browser's cookie (7 days); clearing cookies or switching browsers loses edit and publish rights to it.
- A WhatsApp paid notice can only be sent inside the 24-hour customer-service window (a just-paid booking normally is).
- WhatsApp listing: uploads still in flight when a draft expires can stay in storage (expired collecting drafts are otherwise deleted); if the pipeline's last QStash retry fails, the owner is not told until they send "status".
- Chat acceptance runs use paid model calls and are run on owner approval; the latest results and any open failures are recorded in `docs/plan/06-judge-ready.md`.

## 14. Pages, API routes and configuration

Pages (each under `/en` and `/ar`):

- `/` home and listings
- `/units/[slug]` unit page: photos and fit-out renders per use, "Suitable for" verdicts, specs, nearby places, booking form
- `/units/[slug]/edit` owner edit form (preview-only on demo units)
- `/booking/[id]` booking status, payment button, optional "Get updates on WhatsApp"
- `/chat` web chat with the booking agent
- `/upload` owner video upload (no sign-in; guests get a private draft) with "Try it with a sample walkthrough"
- `/login` sign in with WhatsApp (optional `?next=/<lang>/...` return path)
- `/privacy` (with `#delete` data-deletion section) and `/terms`

API routes (`app/api`):

- `chat`, `chat/voice` (web mic), `bookings`, `availability`, `addons`
- `payments/checkout`, `payments/webhook`
- `whatsapp/webhook`
- `auth/login`, `auth/logout`, `auth/status`, `auth/wa-link` (single-use link from a WhatsApp listing)
- `units`, `units/upload`, `units/specs`, `units/[slug]/stage`, `units/[slug]/pipeline`, `units/[slug]/publish`
- `blob/upload` (client upload tokens), `blob/local` (local media mode only; 404 otherwise), `pipeline/[step]` (QStash step handler)

Environment variable names (values are never committed; see `.env.example`): `META_API_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, `DATABASE_URL_POOLED`, `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN`, `XPAY_SECRET_KEY`, `XPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`, `GUARD_SALT`, `OWNER_SESSION_SECRET`, `DEMO_DAILY_SPEND_USD`, `BOOKING_HOLD_MINUTES`, `OFFISIO_DEV_MODELS`, `MODAL_SPARK_URL`, `MODAL_KEY`, `MODAL_SECRET`, `QSTASH_URL`, `QSTASH_TOKEN`, `QSTASH_CURRENT_SIGNING_KEY`, `QSTASH_NEXT_SIGNING_KEY`, `GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY`, `WHATSAPP_TOKEN`, `WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN`, `WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID`, `WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET`, `WHATSAPP_NUMBER`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SAMPLE_VIDEO_URL` (optional sample walkthrough override). Only `META_API_KEY` and `DATABASE_URL` are required to run. Rate limits can be overridden with `LIMIT_<KIND>_IP` / `LIMIT_<KIND>_GLOBAL`, and model prices with `META_PRICE_*`.

Scripts (`scripts/`, run as `pnpm <name>`): `migrate`, `seed` (`--remote`, `--no-places`), `export-snapshot`, `chat-acceptance`, `check-rubric`, `generate-units`, `remodel-filmed`, `reassess-units`, `stage-units`, `topup-availability`, `backfill-locations`, `places-units`, `brand-assets`; plus `scripts/test-transcribe.ts` (run with `pnpm tsx`).

## 15. Agent testing with curl

Every request below works against the live site or a local copy. Set `B=https://offisio.vercel.app` (or `B=http://localhost:3000`). Keep one cookie jar per "browser" (`-c jar -b jar`): the guest, owner and preview cookies are httpOnly and `Secure` in production. Errors are always `{"error": "<CODE>"}` with an HTTP status; rate limits return 429 with `RATE_LIMITED` (per caller) or `DEMO_QUOTA` (global or spend breaker). Shapes below are read from the route handlers.

### List units

```bash
curl -s "$B/api/units"
curl -s "$B/api/units?slug=gen-alex-chatby"
```

Response: `{"units": [Unit, ...]}`. Unit: `slug`, `kind` (`furnished` | `semifinished`), `district`, `rent_egp`, `daily_egp` (null for long-term units), `floor_text`, `available_from`, `rent_periods` (`daily` | `monthly` | `long_term`), `title_ar`, `title_en`, `summary_ar`, `summary_en`, `highlights_ar`, `highlights_en`, `specs` (object, includes the rubric verdicts), `images` (`{real, empty, staged: [{style, url}]}`), `video`, `synthetic`, `location` (`{lat, lng, approx}` or null), `draft`. The list holds ready, published units only; `?slug=` returns that one unit (an empty array if unknown), and for a draft it has `draft: true`.

### Chat (one Arabic, one English)

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$B/api/chat" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"message":"عايز مكتب في الزمالك ليوم واحد","locale":"ar"}'
curl -s -X POST "$B/api/chat" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"session_id":"<session_id from the first reply>","message":"I want an office near AUC for one day","locale":"en"}'
```

Body: `message` (required, up to 800 characters), `session_id` (optional; omit it to start a session, then send back the returned one), `locale` (`en`, anything else means `ar`). Response: `{"session_id", "reply", "lang", "units": [{slug, title_en, title_ar, district, rent_egp, daily_egp, image, synthetic}], "booking_id"?, "total_egp"?}`. `booking_id` and `total_egp` appear only on the turn that creates a booking; web chat collects name, an Egyptian mobile (`01...`) and an email first, and the booking is an unpaid 30-minute hold. Errors: 400 `EMPTY_MESSAGE` or `MESSAGE_TOO_LONG`; 429 `SESSION_FULL` (20 turns), `RATE_LIMITED`, `DEMO_QUOTA`; 502 on a model failure.

### Booking status

```bash
curl -s "$B/api/bookings?id=<booking_id>"
```

Response: `{"booking": {id, unit_slug, slot_ids, track, rent_egp_total, date, addons: [{id, item_id, name_en, name_ar, qty, unit_price_egp, deliver_at}], total_egp, status, payment_id, created_at, whatsapp_linked, whatsapp_link_url}}`. Renter name, phone, email and WhatsApp id are never returned. `status` is `awaiting_payment` until the signed XPay webhook moves it to `confirmed` (or `payment_failed`, `expired`, `cancelled`, `paid_conflict`). Unknown or malformed id: 404 `NOT_FOUND`.

### Voice turn (web mic)

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$B/api/chat/voice" \
  -F "audio=@note.webm;type=audio/webm" -F "session_id=<optional>" -F "locale=ar"
```

Multipart fields: `audio` (required; webm, ogg/opus, mp4/m4a, aac, mp3 or wav; at most 1 MB and 60 s), `session_id`, `locale`. Order: spend breaker and chat limits, then the voice limit (15 per IP per day), then ffmpeg, then `muse-voice-transcribe-1.0` on `meta.product`, then the same agent turn as `/api/chat`. Response: the `/api/chat` shape plus `"transcript"`. Errors: 400 `VOICE_EMPTY`, 413 `VOICE_TOO_BIG` (also when Content-Length is missing), 415 `VOICE_FORMAT`, 413 `VOICE_TOO_LONG`, 422 `VOICE_UNCLEAR` (no words, or under 0.3 s), 429 `VOICE_LIMIT`, 502 `VOICE_FAILED`. This is a paid call; send short clips.

### Guest upload (no sign-in)

Pick a new slug, e.g. `S=test-$(date +%s)`. Frame files must be `uploads/$S/<name>.jpg` (JPEG, at most 1 MB, 3 to 30 of them); the optional video is `.mp4`, `.mov` or `.webm` (at most 80 MB). The first media request issues the `offisio_guest` cookie, so keep the jar.

Local media mode (local copy without `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN`; returns 404 otherwise):

```bash
for i in 0 1 2; do
  curl -s -c jar -b jar -X PUT "$B/api/blob/local?pathname=uploads/$S/frame-$i.jpg" \
    -H 'content-type: image/jpeg' --data-binary @frame-$i.jpg
done
# each returns {"url": "/uploads/<slug>/frame-<i>.jpg"}
```

With Vercel Blob (live site), the route only issues client tokens:

```bash
curl -s -c jar -b jar -X POST "$B/api/blob/upload" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"type":"blob.generate-client-token","payload":{"pathname":"uploads/'$S'/frame-0.jpg","multipart":false,"clientPayload":null}}'
# {"type":"blob.generate-client-token","clientToken":"..."}
```

The file itself then goes to Vercel Blob with that token; the app does this with `upload()` from `@vercel/blob/client` (`components/UploadForm.tsx`), and the resulting public URL is what `/api/units/upload` expects. For a pure-curl run, the local media mode above is simpler.

Create the unit:

```bash
curl -s -c jar -b jar -X POST "$B/api/units/upload" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "slug":"'$S'","district":"New Administrative Capital","location":"30.036687, 31.681687",
  "rent_egp":14500,"daily_egp":800,"floor_text":"2nd","available_from":"2026-11-10","kind":"furnished",
  "frameUrls":["/uploads/'$S'/frame-0.jpg","/uploads/'$S'/frame-1.jpg","/uploads/'$S'/frame-2.jpg"],
  "frameTimes":[0,1,2]}'
# 202 {"slug": "<slug>"}
```

Fields: `slug`, `district`, `location` ("lat, lng" or a Google Maps link), `rent_egp` (positive integer), `daily_egp` (positive integer or null), `floor_text`, `available_from` (`YYYY-MM-DD`), `kind`, `frameUrls` (Blob URLs, or local `/uploads/<slug>/...` URLs, under this slug), optional `frameTimes` (same length) and `videoUrl`. Furnished units get daily + monthly tracks, semifinished long-term only. Validation errors are 400 with a short message (`LOCATION_INVALID` for a bad location). The unit is a draft: not in `GET /api/units`, not bookable, unknown to the agent. Follow the steps (`analyze`, then listing, renders and `places`) with:

```bash
curl -s "$B/api/units/$S/pipeline"
# {"jobs": [{step, status: queued|running|done|failed, attempts, last_error, updated_at}]}
```

### Publish a draft

```bash
curl -s -c jar -b jar -X POST "$B/api/units/$S/publish" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}'
# {"ok": true, "slug": "<slug>", "mock": false, "ready": true}
```

Needs the uploading browser's guest cookie and a WhatsApp owner session (sign in at `/login` in a browser; the curl jar does not have it). `mock: true` means the local demo publish (WhatsApp not configured, not on Vercel; owner sentinel `local-demo`). `ready: false` means it is listed once the pipeline finishes. Errors: 415 `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE` (not JSON), 401 `SIGN_IN_REQUIRED`, 403 `NOT_DRAFT_OWNER` (another browser), 404 `NOT_FOUND`, 409 `NOT_DRAFT` (already published, or a demo unit).

### Specs edit (preview on demo units)

```bash
curl -s -c jar -b jar -X POST "$B/api/units/specs" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"slug":"gen-alex-chatby","specs":{"desk_capacity":4,"condition":"good"}}'
# demo unit or someone else's unit: {"ok": true, "preview": true}, stored only in the offisio_preview cookie
# your own unit or draft: {"ok": true}, written to the database
curl -s -c jar -b jar -X DELETE "$B/api/units/specs" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}'
# clears the preview cookie: {"ok": true}
```

Allowed `specs` fields: `area_m2_estimate` (5-2000), `desk_capacity` (0-500), `windows_count` (0-100), `ac_units_visible` (0-50), `has_ac` (boolean), `condition` (`excellent`, `good`, `needs_paint`, `needs_work`), `natural_light` (`bright`, `moderate`, `dim`), `flooring` (`tile`, `wood`, `carpet`, `concrete`, `unknown`), `notes_ar` (up to 500 characters); any may be null. Errors: 415 `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`, 400 `SPECS_UNKNOWN_FIELD`, `SPECS_INVALID`, `PREVIEW_TOO_LARGE`, 404 `NOT_FOUND`. Open the unit page with the same cookies to see the preview; the real listing and the agent never change.
